notes.pool: This is the pool, not an intake: the children in these schools, or born in these areas, who will reach this entry point. It does not say how many will come.
notes.counted: Counted: children in these schools now (the January census), followed forward.
notes.notSplitBySex: Not split by sex: girls and boys together.
notes.poolAreaNotSplit: The LA and England lines aren't split by sex, so they are hidden while girls or boys is chosen.
notes.births: Births in the local authority blend; the Reception-to-births ratio sets the range.
notes.birthsScaled: From births: the local authority blend's births, scaled to these schools by the ratio of their Reception pupils to births in past years, then carried forward. A range, not a count.
notes.projection: From ONS projections (age 10, by local authority): a wider band, shown only on request.
notes.birthSplit: Births are counted by calendar year; a school year runs September to August, so each year's pool is 8/12 of one year's births plus 4/12 of the year before.
notes.birthSex: Births have no boy/girl split: a girls' or boys' pool from births is an estimate (49% / 51%).
notes.drift: The range is how much these schools' year groups have actually grown or shrunk from one year to the next since 2019/20 (the middle 80% of those changes), applied for each year still to go -- so it widens the further ahead it looks.
notes.holdShare: The share needed to hold numbers steady: this year's intake as a share of each future pool. A requirement, not a forecast.
notes.groupShare: A share of this group: your pupils at this age as a share of the same age across these schools. Not a share of the local market.
notes.joiners: An estimate: the growth in a year group from one January to the next. It counts net arrivals, not every pupil who joined.
notes.leaving16: Leaving at 16: the fall from Year 11 to Year 12 at the same school, a year apart. An estimate of net leavers.
notes.shape: Shapes describe a school's year groups; they are not better or worse, so they are never ranked.
notes.poolShort: A pipeline shows the pool of children, not who will join. Ranges widen with distance.
notes.localShape: A narrowing base means smaller year groups are on the way.
notes.flagsRule: Flags appear only when a change is large and lasting (fixed national thresholds, over two or more years), never from one small cohort. Hover a flag for the figures behind it.
notes.flagsMissing: Flags not available yet: the national thresholds aren't loaded, and no flag is ever guessed.
notes.feederFlags: Flags compare each school's trend with the area's (the whole set's).
notes.boardingCensus: International boarders aren't in the school census. Your pipeline shows national new joiners to ISC schools by country as context.
notes.areaUndercount: Earlier years count only schools still open, so they slightly undercount.
notes.intakeNote: Two steps that add up to the change: the cohort size (more or fewer local children a year below your entry age) and your share of them. Families moving is part of the cohort size, not a third step. Counts in one area, not a flow of the same children.
notes.intakeMoving: "Families moving" is net: families moving into the area less those moving out, between the earliest age the area's figures hold for the cohort and the year before entry. Children who live outside the radius and travel in to school are not in the area's figures: they show in your share, not in families moving.
notes.intakeBoarding: Boarding schools draw from far beyond any radius: boarders' families are not in this area's figures, so your share here reads high and moves with boarding as well as with the area.
notes.intakeRead: {entryYear} changed by {change}: {cohort} from the cohort size (more or fewer {local}) and {share} from your share of them.
notes.intakeOfWhich: The dashed bar is part of the cohort size, not another step: of its {cohort}, {here} came with the children {hereWords} and {moved} with families {moving} {since} (net).
notes.intakeAveraged: Your intake is small, so each end is a 3-year average.
notes.intakeNotFeeders: The area is your catchment radius, not your feeder list: changing the lists doesn't change this view.
